                                        PROJECT NO. 54445


 REVIEW OF PROTOCOLS ADOPTED                        §    PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 BY THE INDEPENDENT                                 §
                                                                      OF TEXAS
 ORGANIZATION                                       §

                                        PROJECT NO. 59142


 REVIEW OF ERCOT’S                                  §    PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES                          §
                                                                      OF TEXAS
 FOR LARGE LOADS                                    §

  FIRST AMMONIA LLC’S COMMENTS ON COMMISSION CONSIDERATION OF
  PGRR 145, BATCH ZERO PROCESS FOR LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTIONS


       First Ammonia LLC (“First Ammonia”) respectfully submits these comments in Project

No. 54445 (Review of Protocols Adopted by the Independent Organization) and Project No. 59142

(Review of ERCOT Interconnection Process for Large Loads) to inform consideration by the

Public Utility Commission of Texas (“Commission”) of the proposed revision request.


                                   I.      INTRODUCTION

       First Ammonia respectfully requests that the Commission extend the timeline for providing

financial security under proposed Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vi)(C)(1) to December 31 2026,

or to provide its interconnecting transmission service provider (“TSP”), South Texas Electric

Cooperative, Inc. (“STEC”) with the discretion to accept an alternative, collateralized form of

security. The current proposal would require First Ammonia to post more than $117M of financial

security by July 10, 2026 as a Large Load project that qualifies for Base Load inclusion by having

satisfied the requisite study requirements through its ERCOT Regional Planning Group (“RPG”)

endorsement. First Ammonia cannot comply with the financial security requirement within the

existing proposed timeline, on this short notice, preventing its project from qualifying for Base

                                                1
 Load treatment in Batch Zero, despite its legacy status. Failure to be included as Base Load in

Batch Zero will significantly jeopardize the viability of this project, which First Ammonia has

been developing in good faith since 2022 with the cooperation of STEC and its member

distribution cooperative, Victoria Electric Cooperative (“VEC”). Moreover, slipping into Batch

One cannot be considered as a fallback position while no details on Batch One have been made

available. First Ammonia has contributed significant investment in development of its project of

more than $50 million to-date, and successful interconnection of the project stands to contribute

substantial economic benefits to community in which it will operate, contributing to development

in the port of Victoria – the industrial center of Victoria County, Texas, and contributing

substantial tax revenues to the county, including over $3 million annually to the local school

district (Bloomington ISD) alone.

     II.       EXISTING PROPOSED REQUIREMENT AS APPLICABLE TO FIRST
                                    AMMONIA

       First Ammonia qualifies for Base Load treatment under the “complete and valid set of

interconnection studies” consideration in proposed Planning Guide §§ 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(i) and

9.2.1.4(3)(a); namely, First Ammonia’s large load project was included in the study area of one or

more studies submitted to the ERCOT RPG before December 15, 2025, the load contributed to

establishing the need for the RPG transmission project that resolved the performance deficiency

in the study area, and the proposed transmission project received RPG acceptance or ERCOT

endorsement as described in Protocol Section 3.11.4.9, Regional Planning Group Acceptance and

ERCOT Endorsement, on or before March 4, 2026. First Ammonia’s load was submitted to RPG

in May 2025 and received ERCOT Endorsement on February 9, 2026.1



       1
           25RPG012 STEC Ammonia Plant Load Project.

                                                   2
        Under proposed Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vi)(C)(1), the financial security for

transmission upgrades required for Base Load qualification related to an RPG-qualifying project

is determined as follows: “the cost estimate for the total set of Transmission Facility improvements

from the report used as the basis for the RPG acceptance or ERCOT endorsement shall be divided

by the total MW peak Demand of new Large Loads that contribute to establishing the need for the

project to produce a cost per MW estimate. The financial security requirement for the Large Load

shall be the cost per MW estimate multiplied by the peak Demand of the Large Load. If the

Interconnecting DSP or Interconnecting TSP is unable to determine the total MW peak Demand

of new Large Loads contributing to establishing the need for the project, the financial security

requirement for the Large Load shall be $50,000 per MW peak Demand.” This security must be

provided to the interconnecting TSP or distribution service provider (“DSP”) by July 10, 2026. In

First Ammonia’s case, this requires posting of $117.38 million. The ERCOT Board did not

approve PGRR145 until June 2, 2026, leaving First Ammonia with little over one month to comply

with this requirement. Further, the methods of approved financial security are limited to providing

cash collateral, a corporate or parental guaranty (but only if the guarantor meets certain credit

rating requirements), or posting a letter of credit.2 Despite its efforts to comply with these

requirements, First Ammonia has been unable to secure the requisite form of financial security in

the required amount.

               III.    IMPACT ON BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT IN THE STATE

       First Ammonia appreciates that ERCOT has worked diligently to develop a Batch Study

process to facilitate the interconnection of large loads while preserving the reliability of the

ERCOT system. However, we respectfully urge the Commission to consider approval of


       2
           Proposed Planning Guide § § 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(vi)(A)(1)-(3).

                                                         3
 PGRR145 in the context of the Legislature’s charge in Senate Bill 6 (“SB 6”) to establish

interconnection standards large loads in ERCOT “in a manner to support business development in

the state while minimizing the potential for stranded infrastructure costs and maintaining system

reliability.”3 Approval of the new Batch Study process is necessarily an extension of the

Commission’s statutory obligation to develop large load interconnection standards consistent with

SB 6. Unfortunately, the financial security requirements (including the deadline for compliance

therewith) risk business development in the state for large load customers like First Ammonia who

are not major “data center” developers participating in the “AI” boom. First Ammonia’s project is

a green ammonia plant – an end-use large load customer in the traditional sense, which will

consume power for its own retail use, supplied by STEC and VEC. The project has been estimated

to provide a net tax benefit to its community of more than $40M over the next 20 years. First

Ammonia anticipates that the plant will provide more than 100 direct and indirect, new jobs in

Victoria, Texas and will ultimately result in more than $500 million of investment in the county.

The plant will initially produce up to 220,000 metric tons of zero-carbon ammonia annually. This

activity represents First Ammonia’s interest in fostering economic growth in the communities in

which it operates, as well as supporting the hydrogen economy and decarbonization efforts.

        As an end-use industrial customer of energy, First Ammonia is not among the data center

developers who have millions (or even billions) of financial capital at their fingertips. The green

ammonia plant in Victoria, Texas is the first under development in Texas for First Ammonia,

serving as a flagship project for its business in the state. If this project fails to be included in Batch

Zero due to burdensome financial requirements, it is likely that First Ammonia may have to shutter




        3
            PURA § 37.0561(b).

                                                    4
 the project at a significant sunken cost; those costs not being simply transferable to an alternative

site. First Ammonia would inevitably decline to pursue future development in Texas.

       First Ammonia requests that the Commission consider the development of this project to-

date in weighing these comments. Not only has First Ammonia diligently pursued the project,

having successfully received RPG endorsement this Spring and having negotiated in good faith

with STEC and VEC to execute a Facility Extension Agreement for its interconnection, but First

Ammonia has also secured various other permits and agreements required for its development. For

example, the project has obtained all necessary environmental agency permits required to

commence construction. First Ammonia is negotiating the site control agreements required for

Batch Zero inclusion and expects to be able to comply with the related requirements in PGRR145.

The project has been four years in development, and First Ammonia considers it to be integral to

First Ammonia’s goal of advancing a sustainable energy future. The only barrier to the project’s

inclusion in Batch Zero and a path to viability is the financial obligation discussed herein, which

is insurmountable.

                                     IV.     CONCLUSION

       First Ammonia appreciates the Commission’s consideration of these comments. We

respectfully request that the Commission extend the time for RPG-qualifying Base Load projects

to secure the financial security necessary to participate in Batch Zero. We are available to the

Commission to answer any questions or provide further feedback.




Dated: June 17, 2026

                                              Respectfully submitted,



                                                 5
 By:
Joel H. Moser
Chief Executive Officer

FIRST AMMONIA LLC

FOR LARGE LOADS                                   §

      EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF FIRST AMMONIA, LLC’S COMMENTS


 •   First Ammonia LLC (“First Ammonia”) respectfully requests that the Commission extend
     the time for an RPG Base Load-qualifying project to comply with financial security
     obligations beyond July 10, 2026.
 •   First Ammonia respectfully requests that the Commission provide First Ammonia’s
     interconnecting transmission service provider (“TSP”), South Texas Electric Cooperative,
     Inc. (“STEC”) with the discretion to accept an alternative, collateralized form of security.
 •   The existing financial security requirements of PGRR145 for an RPG Base Load-
     qualifying project would require First Ammonia to post security of more than $117M in
     less than one month with limited options for complying with this obligation. This
     represents an insurmountable barrier to entry in Batch Zero for First Ammonia, which is
     developing a green ammonia plant in Victoria County, Texas.
 •   First Ammonia’s large load interconnection project is a traditional end-use large load
     customer, which stands to bring significant economic benefits to Victoria, Texas. The
     project has been under development since 2022, having made significant progress with
     respect to permitting, engineering, logistics, and customer off take, and represents
     significant financial investment for First Ammonia.
 •   If the financial requirements of PGRR145 are not adjusted, First Ammonia will likely be
     forced to abandon its late-stage project, removing business development from the state of
     Texas contrary to the legislative intent of SB6’s large load interconnection standards.
